## Natural history notes

A small tortricid moth characterized by narrow dark brown to blackish forewings with contrasting pale patches or bands that give it a pied, two-toned appearance. In Florida, it is found in wooded and semi-wooded habitats such as hammocks, forest edges, parks, yards, and shrubby areas where suitable host plants and leaf litter occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars likely feed concealed in folded leaves, tied leaves, or plant material, serving as part of the broader food web for spiders, birds, bats, and parasitoid wasps.
